On Wed, Dec 16, 2026 at 11:02 AM Priya wrote:
> Elena — thanks, this is helpful...

Quick notes from the sizing pass (TL;DR below):

Assumptions I used (spreadsheet tab "Sizing v3"):
- Model: open-llama-70b-qat (q4_1 runtime), tokens/sec numbers measured on g5x2-equivalent slab prototype.
- Baseline sustained: 4k t/s. Peak microburst: 26k t/s for 10–20s every 6m.
- Average request length: 40 tokens, tail requests up to 300 tokens (10% of requests).
- KV cache hit rate after warm-up: 84%. Cold-start hit rate initially ~10% for new sessions.

Findings:
- Sustained baseline requires ~1.2 slabs (rounded to 2 slabs for HA) to hit p95 under 250ms with q4_1.
- To safely absorb the 26k t/s microburst without p95 degradation, you need an additional 3 slabs of warm pool capacity (recommendation: reserved + burst pool + pre-warm policy).
- Our headroom recommendation: committed 4 slabs, with a 3-slab burst buffer and autoscale test to verify absorption. That maps to ~7 slabs total peak.

Risk notes:
- Cold-starts can double token processing latency for the first 1–2s of a session; pre-warm and cache-warming (prefetch keys for active users) mitigate this.
- If Nebulonix wants multi-region failover, you should budget an extra 10% compute for cross-region warm replicas.

TL;DR recommendation to share with the customer: commit to 4 slabs (predictable baseline for cost/SLO), maintain a 3-slab burst pool with aggressive pre-warm, and enable cross-region fallback for critical markets.

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Elena — answers inline and added the requested table to the runbook (see attachment).

1) Commitment: yes — with 4 reserved slabs and standard pre-warm policy, measured p95 for sustained 4k t/s is ~210–230ms on our benchmark runs (we include 95% CI in the spreadsheet). We'll include that explicit line in the contract appendix.

2) Burst pool spin-up & cold-starts:
- Spin-up from idle to fully available (cold infra) typically ~60–90s for a new slab allocation.
- If we keep a short warm pool (fractional VMs kept ready) spin-up to warm slab is ~6–12s. That's why we recommend hybrid: reserved 4 slabs + small warm pool + burst autoscale.
- Cold-start latency impact: initially up to 2.5x token time for the first 1–2s per session until KV cache builds. Practically, pre-warm and targeted cache seeding for top 500 active session keys reduces that to ~1.2x after 3s.

Degraded path (if cross-region fallback fails):
- Policy: fallback to smaller quantized variant (q4_0/q2*), enforce shorter context windows for non-critical sessions, and introduce a 10% request sampling to centralized slower region for async processing (with graceful degrade messaging).
- User experience: a subset of sessions will observe higher latency (~500–800ms) and truncated context; critical sessions (flagged by Nebulonix) will always get priority routing to reserved lanes.

Next steps (we'll deliver updated contract appendix table + annotated spreadsheet):
- Priya: share amended runbook PDF with the p95 appendix and the HubSpot link.
- Ben: validate cost delta for keeping a 1-slab warm pool vs. purely on-demand burst.

—Karthik
